source_reviews.independent_solution: Choose unit normal n and signed distance f(X)=n dot X-t. If midpoint is K, f(K)=(f(A)+f(B))/2. A disjoint segment has endpoints with same sign, so d(K,alpha)=(d(A,alpha)+d(B,alpha))/2. An intersecting segment has opposite signs or a zero endpoint, hence d(K,alpha)=abs(d(A,alpha)-d(B,alpha))/2. A segment contained in the plane gives all zeros. This is a proof via affine signed distance, not an assertion about unsigned distances being affine.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Orthogonal projection of an equidistant spatial point is a planar point equidistant from every vertex. (1) Right triangle: all points on the perpendicular to its plane through the hypotenuse midpoint. (2) Isosceles trapezoid is cyclic, so all points on the perpendicular through its circumcenter. (3) A non-square rhombus is not cyclic: opposite angles are equal and cyclicity would require them supplementary, forcing right angles and a square. Therefore the third locus is empty.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Axial symmetry in space is the half-turn about a line p+su. Under the half-turn n becomes 2(u dot n)u-n. To exchange distinct parallel planes requires u dot n=0, and n dot p=(t1+t2)/2. Thus all and only lines contained in the median plane are axes. Their union is that entire plane. An axis perpendicular to the planes leaves their normal coordinate unchanged and cannot exchange them.

source_reviews.independent_solution: (1) Convert 3 dm to 30 cm; put AB=10k, CD=17k. Equal perpendicular components give 100k^2-144=289k^2-900, so k^2=4 and h=sqrt(400-144)=16 cm. (2) If projections p=km, q=kn, then k^2=(a^2-b^2)/(m^2-n^2) and h=sqrt((m^2 b^2-n^2 a^2)/(m^2-n^2)), for m!=n, positive k^2 and positive h^2. If m=n>0, a!=b is impossible; a=b leaves h nonunique (0<h<a for positive projections). (3) For c>0, p+q=c and p^2-q^2=a^2-b^2 give p=(c^2+a^2-b^2)/(2c), q=(c^2-a^2+b^2)/(2c), h=sqrt(((a+b)^2-c^2)*(c^2-(a-b)^2))/(2c). Need p,q>=0 and h>0 for distinct planes; equivalently abs(a^2-b^2)<=c^2<(a+b)^2 (strict lower bound for both projections positive). c=0 is separately possible only if a=b with h=a; these are perpendicular segments.
